titleEn: How Much Does a Bathroom Renovation Cost in Vancouver in 2026?
titleZh: 温哥华卫生间装修价格2026年最新费用详解
contentEn:
Vancouver homeowners spend between $12,000 and $35,000 on a full bathroom renovation in 2026, with the average project landing near $22,000. The wide range reflects choices from a basic refresh to a luxury spa conversion. Understanding where every dollar goes is the first step to budgeting accurately and avoiding the surprise invoices that derail half of all renovation projects in the city.

What Does a Bathroom Renovation Cost in Vancouver?

A standard Vancouver bathroom remodel starts around $12,000 for cosmetic updates — new vanity, tile, fixture, and paint — and climbs to $35,000 or more for a full gut renovation with structural changes, heated floors, and premium finishes. A mid-range renovation with a new walk-in shower, vanity, toilet, and tile flooring typically costs $18,000–$25,000. Every project is priced per square foot of the bathroom being renovated.

  • Cosmetic refresh (new vanity, faucet, paint, tile): $12,000–$18,000
  • Mid-range remodel (walk-in shower, vanity, toilet, flooring): $18,000–$25,000
  • Full gut renovation (plumbing relocation, heated floors, premium finishes): $25,000–$45,000+

Cost Breakdown by Bathroom Element

Labor and installation make up roughly 55–65% of the total budget. The remaining 35–45% goes to materials and fixtures. Here is how costs distribute across the main elements of a typical Vancouver bathroom renovation.

  • Demolition and disposal: $1,200–$3,500 — includes removing old tile, drywall, vanity, toilet, and disposal fees at Metro Vancouver transfer stations.
  • Plumbing rough-in and fixtures: $3,000–$7,000 — new shower pan or tub installation, drain lines, water supply upgrades, new toilet, and faucet.
  • Electrical: $800–$2,500 — pot light installation, GFCI outlets, exhaust fan upgrades, and optional heated floor wiring.
  • Tile and waterproofing: $2,500–$6,000 — floor and shower wall tile, waterproofing membrane, grout, and sealant. Porcelain tile averages $4–$12 per square foot installed.
  • Vanity and countertops: $1,500–$4,500 — solid wood or engineered wood vanity ($800–$2,500) plus quartz or granite countertop ($700–$2,000).
  • Paint and finishing: $400–$900 — bathroom-grade mold-resistant paint on ceiling and walls, usually one to two gallons.
  • Permit fees: $200–$600 — City of Vancouver plumbing and building permit fees for bathroom alterations. Relocating plumbing fixtures requires a full building permit.

City-Specific Factors That Affect Vancouver Bathroom Costs

Vancouver building code, strata requirements, and supply chain conditions add costs that do not apply equally across other Canadian cities. A renovation in a Coquitlam condo faces different rules than a West Vancouver house.

  • City of Vancouver permit requirements: Moving any plumbing fixture — a toilet, sink, or shower — requires a building permit in Vancouver. A cosmetic refresh with no plumbing changes may qualify for an expedite permit, saving $200–$400.
  • Strata approval in condos and townhouses: Properties in Burnaby, Richmond, and Vancouver condo towers require strata approval before work begins. The process adds two to six weeks and a $200–$500 strata administration fee.
  • Material availability: Imported tile and premium fixtures face ongoing supply delays of four to ten weeks. Ordering early prevents timeline extensions that cost $500–$1,500 in temporary accommodation or alternative arrangements.
  • Disposal fees at Metro Vancouver transfer stations: A full bathroom gut generates approximately one to two tonnes of construction debris. Disposal costs $150–$350 depending on weight and bin rental.

How Long Does a Bathroom Renovation Take in Vancouver?

A mid-range bathroom renovation in Vancouver takes six to nine weeks from demolition to final inspection. The City of Vancouver schedules plumbing and building inspections within three to five business days of request, which keeps most projects on pace. Strata approvals and permit delays add two to eight weeks on top of the construction timeline.

  • Cosmetic refresh: 2–4 weeks
  • Mid-range remodel: 6–9 weeks
  • Full gut renovation: 10–16 weeks

How to Budget for Your Vancouver Bathroom Renovation

Add a 15–20% contingency to every Vancouver bathroom renovation budget. Unexpected discoveries — water damage behind old tile, outdated wiring, or corroded supply pipes — appear in approximately 40% of Vancouver bathroom projects and routinely cost $2,000–$5,000 to repair before work can continue. A realistic budget with a contingency prevents the choice between stopping mid-project or cutting scope unexpectedly.

What is the average cost of a bathroom renovation in Vancouver in 2026?

The average bathroom renovation in Vancouver costs approximately $22,000 in 2026 for a mid-range project with a walk-in shower, new vanity, toilet, and tile flooring. Cosmetic updates start around $12,000; full gut renovations with premium finishes and plumbing relocation range from $25,000 to $45,000 or more.

Do I need a permit for a bathroom renovation in Vancouver?

You need a building permit in Vancouver whenever you move or alter plumbing fixtures — a toilet, sink, or shower. Cosmetic work that does not change plumbing configuration may qualify for an expedite permit. The City of Vancouver charges $200–$600 in permit fees depending on project scope. Always confirm permit requirements before starting work.

How long does a bathroom renovation take in Vancouver?

A mid-range bathroom renovation in Vancouver takes six to nine weeks from demolition to final inspection. Strata approvals for condo and townhouse projects add two to six weeks. Full gut renovations with plumbing relocation take ten to sixteen weeks. Permit and inspection waiting times are typically three to five business days per inspection in the City of Vancouver.

What percentage of a bathroom renovation budget goes to labour?

Labour and installation make up 55–65% of the total bathroom renovation budget in Vancouver. The remaining 35–45% covers materials and fixtures. Demolition, plumbing, electrical, tiling, and finishing work are the largest labour line items.

Should I include a contingency budget for a Vancouver bathroom renovation?

Add a 15–20% contingency to every Vancouver bathroom renovation budget. Approximately 40% of Vancouver bathroom projects uncover unexpected issues such as water damage, outdated electrical wiring, or corroded pipes behind existing walls. A $22,000 project should include $3,300–$4,400 in contingency funds to cover these discoveries without stopping work.

温哥华卫生间装修费用明细

温哥华标准的卫生间改造起步价约为$12,000加元，适用于表面翻新——更换洗手台、瓷砖、洁具和油漆；全面改造加上结构变更、加热地板和高端装修则可能达到$35,000加元以上。中档改造（包含步入式淋浴间、洗手台、马桶和地板砖）通常费用在$18,000至$25,000加元之间。每个项目的报价均按所装修卫生间的面积计算。

  • 表面翻新（新洗手台、水龙头、油漆、瓷砖）：$12,000–$18,000
  • 中档改造（步入式淋浴间、洗手台、马桶、地板）：$18,000–$25,000
  • 全拆重建（管道移位、加热地板、高端装修）：$25,000–$45,000+

各项目费用明细

人工和安装费用约占总预算的55%至65%，其余35%至45%用于材料采购。以下是温哥华典型卫生间改造各主要项目的费用分配。

  • 拆除及垃圾清运：$1,200–$3,500 — 包括拆除旧瓷砖、石膏板、洗手台、马桶，以及大温哥华转运站的处置费用。
  • 管道预埋及洁具：$3,000–$7,000 — 新淋浴盘或浴缸安装、排水管线、供水系统升级、新马桶及水龙头。
  • 电气工程：$800–$2,500 — 筒灯安装、GFCI插座、排气扇升级，以及可选的加热地板布线。
  • 瓷砖及防水工程：$2,500–$6,000 — 地板和淋浴墙瓷砖、防水膜、水泥浆和密封剂。瓷板砖平均$4–$12/平方尺（含人工）。
  • 浴室柜及台面：$1,500–$4,500 — 实木或工程木浴室柜（$800–$2,500）加石英石或花岗岩台面（$700–$2,000）。
  • 油漆及收尾：$400–$900 — 卫生间防霉油漆，通常一至两罐。
  • 许可证费用：$200–$600 — 温哥华市管道及建筑许可证费用。移动管道设施需申请全面建筑许可。

影响温哥华卫生间装修费用的本地因素

温哥华建筑规范、物业管理规定和供应链状况会增加其他加拿大城市未必适用的费用。高贵林公寓的装修规则与西温独立屋截然不同。

  • 温哥华市许可证要求：在温哥华，移动任何管道设施（马桶、水槽或淋浴间）均需申请建筑许可。不涉及管道改动的表面翻新可申请快速许可，节省$200–$400。
  • 公寓及联排别墅物业管理审批：本拿比、列治文和温哥华公寓楼的物业需在工程开工前获得物业管理批准。整个流程额外需要两至六周，并产生$200–$500的物业管理费。
  • 材料供应情况：进口瓷砖和高端洁具目前面临四至十周的持续供货延迟。提前下单可避免导致额外$500–$1,500临时住宿或替代安排费用的工期延误。
  • 大温哥华转运站处置费：全套卫生间拆除约产生一至两吨建筑垃圾。根据重量和垃圾箱租赁，处置费用为$150–$350。

温哥华卫生间装修需要多长时间？

温哥华中档卫生间改造从拆除到最终验收大约需要六至九周。温哥华市会在申请后三至五个工作日内安排管道和建筑验收，保持大多数项目的进度。物业管理审批和许可延误则在其基础上额外增加两至八周。

  • 表面翻新：2–4周
  • 中档改造：6–9周
  • 全拆重建：10–16周

如何为温哥华卫生间装修做预算

为每个温哥华卫生间装修预算增加15%至20%的应急资金。约40%的温哥华卫生间项目会发现意外问题——旧瓷砖后面的水损坏、线路老化或管道腐蚀——这些问题通常需要$2,000至$5,000加元进行修复，才能继续施工。有了应急资金的真实预算，才能避免项目中途停工或被迫削减规模的困境。
